title: The Codex Gigas Mystery
hook: Who actually wrote the Devil's Bible?
headline: The Book That Brought the Devil

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: In the early 13th century, monks at the Benedictine monastery of Podlažice near Chrast, Bohemia created the massive manuscript.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: The manuscript contains a single full-page portrait of the Devil; the book is 92 cm long, not 92 pages, and the legend attributes the whole codex to Herman the Recluse.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: A 200-year-old legend claims the scribe bargained with the devil for the book's completion.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: Radiocarbon testing in 2015 dated the vellum to the early 1200s, confirming its medieval origin.

end.line: Could a pact truly explain this massive tome?

description: Explore the mysterious origins of the massive medieval manuscript known as the Devil's Bible.

facts.claim: The Codex Gigas was created in the early 13th century at a Benedictine monastery in Kutna Hora, Bohemia
The manuscript contains a 92-page illuminated portrait of the Devil
Legend attributes the work to a monk named Herman the Recluse who allegedly made a pact with the Devil
Radiocarbon dating performed in 2015 placed the vellum's origin in the early 1200s
The Codex Gigas measures about 92 cm tall, making it the largest surviving medieval manuscript

unsupported: The legend is 200 years old
